proofs.proof_tex:
Assume the affirmative content of
\(\mathrm{oeq{:}fixed\text{-}nuisance\text{-}marked\text{-}modulus}\).
Then there are constants \(\eta\in(0,1-2\alpha)\),
\(c_{\mathrm{sep}}>0\), and \(n_0<\infty\) such that, for every
\(n\ge n_0\), the laws \(P_{0,n},P_{1,n}\) belong to \(\mathcal M\) and
\[
 Q_{j,n}:=((P_{j,n})_{\mathrm{obs}})^{\otimes n},\qquad
 \operatorname{TV}(Q_{0,n},Q_{1,n})\le\eta,
 \qquad
 \Delta_n:=\|\mu_{1,n}-\mu_{0,n}\|_{L^\infty(I)}
 \ge c_{\mathrm{sep}}K_n^{1/2-\beta}.                              \tag{1}
\]
Fix such an \(n\) and any
\(\mathcal C_n=(L_n,U_n)\in\mathfrak B_{n,\alpha}\).  Define
\[
 H_{j,n}=\{L_n(a)\le\mu_{j,n}(a)\le U_n(a)
             \text{ for every }a\in I\},\qquad j=0,1.              \tag{2}
\]
Since \(P_{j,n}\in\mathcal M\), honesty gives
\(Q_{j,n}(H_{j,n})\ge1-\alpha\).  The defining event inequality for total
variation and (1) imply
\[
 Q_{0,n}(H_{1,n})
 \ge Q_{1,n}(H_{1,n})-\operatorname{TV}(Q_{0,n},Q_{1,n})
 \ge1-\alpha-\eta.                                                  \tag{3}
\]
Thus
\[
 Q_{0,n}(H_{0,n}\cap H_{1,n})
 \ge1-2\alpha-\eta.                                                 \tag{4}
\]
On the intersection in (4), each interval \([L_n(a),U_n(a)]\) contains both
curves, so
\[
 W_n\ge\sup_{a\in I}|\mu_{1,n}(a)-\mu_{0,n}(a)|=\Delta_n.           \tag{5}
\]
Since \(W_n\ge0\) by \(\mathrm{def{:}honest\text{-}bands}\), equations
(1), (4), and (5) give
\[
 E_{Q_{0,n}}[W_n]
 \ge(1-2\alpha-\eta)c_{\mathrm{sep}}K_n^{1/2-\beta}.               \tag{6}
\]
The coefficient
\(c'=(1-2\alpha-\eta)c_{\mathrm{sep}}\) is strictly positive.  Since
\(P_{0,n}\in\mathcal M\), taking first the supremum over \(P\in\mathcal M\)
and then the infimum over honest bands proves the stated lower bound.

For the scale comparison, put \(x_n=\log n/\log\log n\) and
\(\gamma=\beta-1/2>0\).  For all sufficiently large \(n\),
\(x_n/2\le K_n=\lfloor x_n\rfloor\le x_n\).  Therefore
\[
 x_n^{-\gamma}\le K_n^{-\gamma}\le2^\gamma x_n^{-\gamma},
 \qquad
 x_n^{-\gamma}
 =\left(\frac{\log\log n}{\log n}\right)^{\beta-1/2}=r_n.
\]
Hence \(K_n^{1/2-\beta}\asymp r_n\), completing the conditional proof.

added_lemmas.statement:
Equip \(\mathscr K\) with the product of Euclidean distance for \((p_x)_x\),
uniform distance on \(\mathcal A\) for every \(f_x,q_x\), and any metric for
weak convergence of \(Q_1,Q_2\).  Then \(\mathscr K\) is compact.  Along
convergent sequences in this metric, \(\phi_{Q_j}\) converges uniformly on
every compact frequency interval, the fitted probability and marked channels
converge locally uniformly on \(\mathbb R^2\), and
\(\vartheta\mapsto\mu_\vartheta\) is continuous from \(\mathscr K\) to
\(C(I)\).  For every \(n\), the exact feasible set
\(\Theta^{\mathrm{ex}}_{n,\alpha}(z)\) is compact, and its finitely many
constraint-violation functions are measurable in \(z\) and continuous in
\(\vartheta\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Write the Fourier norm in the equivalent form
\[
 \|g\|_{H^\beta}^2
 =\frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{\mathbb R}(1+t^2)^\beta
 |\widehat g(t)|^2\,dt.
\]
The fixed convention-dependent constant is immaterial.  For smooth integrable
\(g\), the defining Fourier integral and Cauchy--Schwarz give, for
\(a,b\in\mathbb R\),
\[
 |g(a)-g(b)|
 \le \frac{R}{\sqrt{2\pi}}
 \left\{\int_{\mathbb R}
 |e^{-ita}-e^{-itb}|^2(1+t^2)^{-\beta}\,dt\right\}^{1/2}.       \tag{1}
\]
Approximation in the weighted Fourier norm extends (1) to the whole Sobolev
ball.  Because \(\beta>3/2>1/2\), the dominating function
\(4(1+t^2)^{-\beta}\) is integrable, and the integral in (1) tends to zero
as \(|a-b|\to0\), uniformly over the corresponding Sobolev ball.  The same
Cauchy--Schwarz calculation with \(b\) omitted gives a uniform supremum
bound.  A finite spatial mesh on the compact interval \(\mathcal A\), followed
by a finite quantization of the bounded function values on that mesh, now
gives a finite uniform net.  Thus each of the two bounded Sobolev balls is
totally bounded in \(C(\mathcal A)\).

For completeness, the uniform limits stay in the asserted Sobolev balls.
Indeed, from any bounded sequence put
\(h_m(t)=(1+t^2)^{\beta/2}\widehat g_m(t)\).  Expanding in a fixed countable
orthonormal basis of \(L^2(\mathbb R)\), successively selecting convergent
coefficient subsequences, and applying the bound to every finite partial sum
produces a weak limit \(h\) with
\(\|h\|_2\le\liminf_m\|h_m\|_2\).  Testing against compactly supported
Fourier functions identifies the corresponding inverse transform with the
uniform limit on \(\mathcal A\).  It follows that the limit is in
\(H^\beta(\mathbb R)\), has norm at most the same radius, and vanishes almost
everywhere outside \(\mathcal A\).  Its continuous representative therefore
has the required support.  Uniform convergence also preserves nonnegativity,
unit integral, the lower bound on \(I\), and the inequality
\(|q_x|\le B_Yf_x\).  Consequently the signal portion of \(\mathscr K\) is
compact in the declared uniform topology.  The finite-dimensional mass
simplex with \(p_x\ge p_{\min}\) is compact as well.

It remains to treat the error laws.  Their moment restriction implies the
uniform tail bound
\[
 Q_j(|u|>R)\le M_eR^{-q_e}.                                      \tag{2}
\]
Given any sequence of such laws, successively partition each compact interval
\([-r,r]\) into finitely many rational half-open intervals and diagonally
select a subsequence on which all cell masses converge.  Consistency under
refinement and (2) define a probability law \(Q_j\), and upper and lower step
approximations to a bounded continuous function show weak convergence to that
law.  For every \(M<\infty\), weak convergence applied to the bounded
continuous function \(|u|^{q_e}\wedge M\), followed by monotone convergence,
gives
\[
 \int|u|^{q_e}\,dQ_j(u)\le M_e.                                  \tag{3}
\]
Moreover, uniformly over the sequence,
\[
 \int_{|u|>R}|u|\,dQ_j(u)
 \le M_eR^{1-q_e}\longrightarrow0.                               \tag{4}
\]
Truncating the identity function and using (4) proves convergence of first
moments.  Hence the centering condition for \(Q_2\) is closed.

For \(|s-t|\le\delta\), the moment bound and Jensen's inequality imply
\[
 |\phi_{Q_j}(s)-\phi_{Q_j}(t)|
 \le |s-t|\int|u|\,dQ_j(u)
 \le \delta M_e^{1/q_e}.                                         \tag{5}
\]
Weak convergence gives pointwise convergence of characteristic functions;
the common modulus (5) upgrades it, by a finite frequency net, to uniform
convergence on every compact interval.  It also shows that the protected
local-modulus constraint is closed.  Equations (2)--(5) prove compactness of
the error-law portion, and hence of the finite product \(\mathscr K\).

Uniform convergence of \(f_x,q_x\), their common compact support, and local
uniform convergence of the characteristic functions show directly that
\[
 \widehat f_x(s+t)\phi_{Q_1}(s)\phi_{Q_2}(t),\qquad
 \widehat q_x(s+t)\phi_{Q_1}(s)\phi_{Q_2}(t)                       \tag{6}
\]
converge locally uniformly in \((s,t)\).  Since every denominator is at least
\(\kappa\) on \(I\), for two tuples \(\vartheta,\vartheta'\),
\[
 \left\|\frac{q_x}{f_x}-\frac{q'_x}{f'_x}\right\|_{L^\infty(I)}
 \le \kappa^{-1}\|q_x-q'_x\|_\infty
     +B_Y\kappa^{-1}\|f_x-f'_x\|_\infty.                         \tag{7}
\]
Combining (7) with convergence of the finite mass vector proves continuity of
\(\vartheta\mapsto\mu_\vartheta\) into \(C(I)\).

Finally, at fixed \(n\) the exact feasibility restrictions are finitely many
weak inequalities involving the continuous maps in (6), together with the
closed mass-region inequalities.  They therefore cut out a closed, hence
compact, subset of \(\mathscr K\).  The empirical transforms, counts, and
radii are measurable in the sample, while the fitted sides are continuous in
\(\vartheta\).  Taking the maximum of the positive parts of these finitely
many violations proves the last assertion.
added_lemmas.justification: Compactness is the deterministic substitute for a quantitative inverse modulus in the exact projected nuisance class.
added_lemmas.gap: The finite relaxed sieve does not have a proved shrinking diameter, whereas exact class constraints admit a qualitative subsequence argument.
added_lemmas.consumer: It supplies compact feasible values, continuous target profiling, and convergent subsequences for the qualitative diameter lemma and abstract exact-class band.

added_lemmas.statement:
For a realized sample \(z\), write \(n_x(z)\) for its stratum counts and set
\[
 \omega_n=
 \sup_{\substack{z:\ \min_{x\in\mathcal X}n_x(z)\ge np_{\min}/2,\\
                  \Theta^{\mathrm{ex}}_{n,\alpha}(z)\ne\varnothing}}
 \operatorname{diam}_{L^\infty(I)}
 \{\mu_\vartheta:\vartheta\in
 \Theta^{\mathrm{ex}}_{n,\alpha}(z)\},                           \tag{1}
\]
with the supremum defined as zero if its indexing set is empty.  Then
\(\omega_n\to0\).  This conclusion is deterministic and qualitative; it
asserts neither an explicit modulus nor an \(O(r_n)\) bound.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Suppose, to the contrary, that (1) does not tend to zero.  Then there are
\(\epsilon>0\), integers \(n_k\to\infty\), realized samples \(z_k\) with
regular counts, and two feasible tuples
\(\vartheta_k,\vartheta'_k\in
\Theta^{\mathrm{ex}}_{n_k,\alpha}(z_k)\) such that
\[
 \|\mu_{\vartheta_k}-\mu_{\vartheta'_k}\|_{L^\infty(I)}
 \ge\epsilon.                                                       \tag{2}
\]
The exact-class compactness lemma permits passage to a common subsequence on
which
\[
 \vartheta_k\longrightarrow\vartheta,
 \qquad
 \vartheta'_k\longrightarrow\vartheta'                             \tag{3}
\]
in the product topology of that lemma.

Both mass vectors belong to the same mass region.  Therefore
\[
 \max_{x\in\mathcal X}|p_{x,k}-p'_{x,k}|
 \le2\left\{\frac{\log(6|\mathcal X|/\alpha)}{2n_k}\right\}^{1/2}
 \longrightarrow0,                                                  \tag{4}
\]
so the limiting mass vectors in (3) are equal.  Next, the tuning definitions
give
\[
 |\mathcal D_n|=(2K_n^2+1)^2,
 \qquad
 \lambda_n=O(\log K_n)=o(n).                                       \tag{5}
\]
On the regular-count samples, (5) and the definitions of the empirical radii
imply
\[
 \max_x\rho^F_{x,n_k}\le
 2\left(\frac{2\lambda_{n_k}}{n_kp_{\min}}\right)^{1/2}=o(1),
 \qquad
 \max_x\rho^G_{x,n_k}\le B_Y\max_x\rho^F_{x,n_k}=o(1).            \tag{6}
\]

Denote the two fitted channels of a tuple by
\[
 F_{x,\vartheta}(s,t)=
 \widehat f_x(s+t)\phi_{Q_1}(s)\phi_{Q_2}(t),
 \qquad
 G_{x,\vartheta}(s,t)=
 \widehat q_x(s+t)\phi_{Q_1}(s)\phi_{Q_2}(t).                      \tag{7}
\]
Because \(|A|\le B_A\) under every candidate signal law and
\(\int|u|\,dQ_j(u)\le M_e^{1/q_e}\), the elementary inequality
\(|e^{iv}-e^{iw}|\le|v-w|\) gives one constant \(C<\infty\), depending
only on the fixed class indices, such that
\[
 |F_{x,\vartheta}(s,t)-F_{x,\vartheta}(s',t')|
 \le C(|s-s'|+|t-t'|),                                             \tag{8}
\]
uniformly over \(\vartheta\in\mathscr K\).  The same calculation against the
signed measure \(q_x(a)\,da\), using
\(\int|q_x|\le B_Y\), gives (8) with \(G\) in place of \(F\), after
enlarging \(C\).

At every grid point, feasibility around the same empirical transform and the
triangle inequality yield
\[
 |F_{x,\vartheta_k}-F_{x,\vartheta'_k}|le2\rho^F_{x,n_k},
 \qquad
 |G_{x,\vartheta_k}-G_{x,\vartheta'_k}|le2\rho^G_{x,n_k}.           \tag{9}
\]
The grid \(\Gamma_{n_k}\) has mesh \((B_AK_{n_k})^{-1}\) and range
\(K_{n_k}/B_A\to\infty\).  For any fixed \((s,t)\), choose a nearest grid
point for all sufficiently large \(k\).  Equations (6), (8), and (9) show
that the difference of the two fitted probability channels, and separately
of the two fitted marked channels, tends to zero at \((s,t)\).  Passing to
the limits in (3) by local uniform channel convergence gives
\[
 F_{x,\vartheta}(s,t)=F_{x,\vartheta'}(s,t),
 \qquad
 G_{x,\vartheta}(s,t)=G_{x,\vartheta'}(s,t)                         \tag{10}
\]
for every \(x\in\mathcal X\) and \((s,t)\in\mathbb R^2\).

We now prove, rather than assume, that (10) identifies the exact projected
signals.  Fix a cell \(x\), and write \(\widetilde f_x,\widetilde q_x\) for
the signal components of \(\vartheta'\).  Every candidate has
\(\widehat f_x(0)=\widehat{\widetilde f}_x(0)=1\); continuity gives a
neighborhood \(J\) of zero on which both limiting latent transforms are
nonzero.  Shrink \(J\) so that
\(J\subset(-\nu_0,\nu_0)\).  The protected-modulus restriction makes both
error characteristic functions nonzero there.  The moment restriction makes
them differentiable at zero, and centering gives
\[
 \phi'_{Q_2}(0)=i\int u\,dQ_2(u)=0,
 \qquad
 \phi'_{Q'_2}(0)=0.                                                 \tag{11}
\]
For \(u\in J\), differentiate the first equality in (10) with respect to
its second argument at \((u,0)\), divide by its nonzero value there, and use
(11).  This yields
\[
 \frac{\widehat f'_x(u)}{\widehat f_x(u)}
 =\left.\frac{\partial_tF_{x,\vartheta}(u,t)}
 {F_{x,\vartheta}(u,t)}\right|_{t=0}
 =\left.\frac{\partial_tF_{x,\vartheta'}(u,t)}
 {F_{x,\vartheta'}(u,t)}\right|_{t=0}
 =\frac{\widehat{\widetilde f}_x'(u)}
        {\widehat{\widetilde f}_x(u)},                              \tag{12}
\]
where derivatives are with respect to \(u\).  Equivalently, the derivative
of \(\widehat f_x/\widehat{\widetilde f}_x\) is zero on \(J\).  Its
value at zero is one, so
\[
 \widehat f_x(u)=\widehat{\widetilde f}_x(u),\qquad u\in J.         \tag{13}
\]
Compact support makes both sides entire.  Applied to their difference,
successive real differentiation inside \(J\) makes every Taylor coefficient
at an interior point zero; overlapping Taylor discs then extend (13) to all
complex arguments.  To see directly that equality of the Fourier transforms
implies equality of the densities, put \(h=f_x-\widetilde f_x\) and let
\(\gamma_\sigma\) be the centered Gaussian density with variance
\(\sigma^2\).  Absolute integrability permits exchanging the two integrals,
and the explicit Gaussian integral gives
\[
 (h*\gamma_\sigma)(a)
 =\frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{\mathbb R}e^{-ita}
   \widehat h(t)e^{-\sigma^2t^2/2}\,dt=0.                           \tag{13a}
\]
On the other hand,
\[
 \|h*\gamma_\sigma-h\|_1
 \le\int\gamma_\sigma(y)\|h(\,\cdot-y)-h\|_1\,dy\longrightarrow0. \tag{13b}
\]
Here translation continuity follows first by direct calculation for indicators
of bounded intervals, then for finite linear combinations of such indicators,
and finally for \(h\in L^1\) by approximation; the integrand is bounded by
\(2\|h\|_1\), and the Gaussian mass concentrates at zero.  Thus
\(f_x=\widetilde f_x\) in \(L^1\), hence everywhere for their continuous
representatives.

For \(u\) in a possibly smaller neighborhood of zero, (10) and (13) give
\[
 \widehat q_x(u)
 =\widehat f_x(u)\frac{G_{x,\vartheta}(u,0)}
                         {F_{x,\vartheta}(u,0)}
 =\widehat{\widetilde f}_x(u)\frac{G_{x,\vartheta'}(u,0)}
                          {F_{x,\vartheta'}(u,0)}
 =\widehat{\widetilde q}_x(u).                                     \tag{14}
\]
The two signed densities also have compact support, so the same Taylor-disc
and Gaussian-convolution argument applied to (14) yields
\(q_x=\widetilde q_x\).
This holds in every cell.  Together with (4), the two limiting tuples have
the same target function.

Finally, continuity of the target map from the exact-class compactness lemma
and (3) imply
\[
 \|\mu_{\vartheta_k}-\mu_{\vartheta'_k}\|_{L^\infty(I)}
 \longrightarrow
 \|\mu_\vartheta-\mu_{\vartheta'}\|_{L^\infty(I)}=0,
\]
contradicting (2).  Hence \(\omega_n\to0\).
added_lemmas.justification: This is the qualitative inverse result needed to turn exact empirical-channel feasibility into uniformly shrinking expected width.
added_lemmas.gap: It proves only vanishing diameter and deliberately supplies no numerical modulus or logarithmic rate.
added_lemmas.consumer: It is the deterministic width input for the abstract exact-class honest band.

added_lemmas.statement:
There exists \(n_0<\infty\), depending only on \(\alpha\) and the fixed class
indices, such that for every \(n\ge n_0\) the abstract exact-class band
\(\mathcal C_n^{\mathrm{ex}}\) has jointly sample-and-index measurable finite
endpoints, belongs to \(\mathfrak B_{n,\alpha}\), and satisfies
\[
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal M}P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}
 \{L_n^{\mathrm{ex}}(a)\le\mu(a)\le U_n^{\mathrm{ex}}(a)
 \text{ for every }a\in I\}\ge1-\alpha,
 \qquad 0\le W_n^{\mathrm{ex}}\le2B_Y.
\]
Moreover, with \(\omega_n\) from
\(\mathrm{lem{:}qualitative\text{-}exact\text{-}grid\text{-}diameter}\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M}
 E_{P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}}[W_n^{\mathrm{ex}}]
 \le \omega_n+2B_Y|\mathcal X|e^{-np_{\min}/8}=o(1).
\]
The construction is qualitative and noncomputational; no explicit rate,
\(O(r_n)\) conclusion, or minimax claim is asserted.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
We first establish measurability.  By
\(\mathrm{lem{:}exact\text{-}class\text{-}compactness}\),
\(\mathscr K\) is a compact metric space.  Let
\(h(z,\vartheta)\) be the maximum of zero and the positive parts of all mass
and channel constraint violations defining
\(\Theta^{\mathrm{ex}}_{n,\alpha}(z)\).  Then \(h\) is measurable in the
sample \(z\), continuous in \(\vartheta\), and
\[
 \Theta^{\mathrm{ex}}_{n,\alpha}(z)
 =\{\vartheta\in\mathscr K:h(z,\vartheta)=0\}.                      \tag{1}
\]
Let \(K_0\) be a countable dense subset of \(\mathscr K\).  Continuity gives
\[
 d(z):=\inf_{\vartheta\in\mathscr K}h(z,\vartheta)
      =\inf_{\vartheta\in K_0}h(z,\vartheta),                      \tag{2}
\]
so \(d\) is measurable; compactness shows that the feasible set is nonempty
exactly when \(d=0\).  On that event, define
\[
 V_m^+(z,a)=\sup_{\vartheta\in\mathscr K}
 \{\mu_\vartheta(a)-m h(z,\vartheta)\},
\]
and define \(V_m^-\) with \(-\mu_\vartheta\) in place of
\(\mu_\vartheta\).  Each supremum may be taken over \(K_0\), hence is jointly
measurable in \((z,a)\).  Compactness and continuity imply
\[
 V_m^+(z,a)\downarrow
 \sup_{\vartheta\in\Theta^{\mathrm{ex}}_{n,\alpha}(z)}
 \mu_\vartheta(a),
 \qquad
 V_m^-(z,a)\downarrow
 -\inf_{\vartheta\in\Theta^{\mathrm{ex}}_{n,\alpha}(z)}
 \mu_\vartheta(a).                                                 \tag{3}
\]
Indeed, maximizers exist; boundedness of \(\mu_\vartheta(a)\) and comparison
with a feasible tuple force their violations to zero, and every convergent
subsequence has a feasible limit.  The reverse inequalities in (3) follow by
evaluating at feasible tuples.  Equations (2)--(3), the zero convention on an
empty set, and deterministic clipping prove joint measurability of the two
endpoints.  The exact-class compactness lemma also makes the unprofiled extrema
continuous in \(a\); hence the supremum defining \(W_n^{\mathrm{ex}}\) can be
taken over a fixed countable dense subset of \(I\), proving its measurability.
Every candidate obeys \(|q_x/f_x|\le B_Y\) on \(I\), and its masses form a
simplex.  Thus
\[
 |\mu_\vartheta(a)|\le B_Y.                                        \tag{4}
\]
Consequently clipping preserves endpoint ordering whenever the feasible set
is nonempty; the empty-set convention does so otherwise.  The endpoints are
finite and
\[
 0\le W_n^{\mathrm{ex}}\le2B_Y                                    \tag{5}
\]
for every sample.

Fix \(P\in\mathcal M\).  Its projected tuple
\[
 \vartheta_P=((p_x,f_x,q_x)_{x\in\mathcal X},
               \mathcal L_P(U_1),\mathcal L_P(U_2))                \tag{6}
\]
belongs to \(\mathscr K\).  Indeed, the mass, support, Sobolev, denominator,
moment, centering, and local-modulus restrictions are the corresponding
conditions in \(\mathrm{def{:}model\text{-}class}\).  Consistency and the
bounded structural response imply
\(|E_P[Y\mid A=a,X=x]|\le B_Y\) almost everywhere; since
\(q_x=m_xf_x\), this gives \(|q_x|\le B_Yf_x\) almost everywhere and hence
everywhere for the continuous representatives.  The support condition for
\(q_x\) follows from that for \(f_x\).

On the event \(\mathcal E_{n,\alpha}\), the true mass vector lies in
\(\mathcal P_{n,\alpha}\), and the exact factorization in
\(\mathrm{lem{:}factorization}\) turns the empirical-channel inequalities
in that event into exactly the residual inequalities defining
\(\Theta^{\mathrm{ex}}_{n,\alpha}\).  Therefore
\[
 \mathcal E_{n,\alpha}
 \subseteq\{\vartheta_P\in\Theta^{\mathrm{ex}}_{n,\alpha}\}.       \tag{7}
\]
The ADRF identification theorem gives
\(\mu=\mu_{\vartheta_P}\) on \(I\).  Equations (4) and (7) then show that,
on \(\mathcal E_{n,\alpha}\), profiling and clipping contain \(\mu(a)\)
simultaneously for every \(a\in I\).  The confidence-event conclusion of
\(\mathrm{lem{:}analytic\text{-}sieve\text{-}stability}\) supplies, for all
sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal M}P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}
 (\mathcal E_{n,\alpha})\ge1-\alpha.                               \tag{8}
\]
Thus the band has the required uniform coverage; measurability, ordering, and
finiteness already proved above verify every clause of
\(\mathrm{def{:}honest\text{-}bands}\).

Let
\(R_n=\{\min_{x\in\mathcal X}n_x\ge np_{\min}/2\}\).  On \(R_n\), an empty
feasible set has zero width, while a nonempty one has width bounded by the
diameter in the definition of \(\omega_n\).  Hence
\[
 W_n^{\mathrm{ex}}\mathbf 1_{R_n}
 \le\omega_n.                                                       \tag{9}
\]
On \(R_n^c\), use (5).  The count inequality in
\(\mathrm{lem{:}mass\text{-}confidence}\) and (9) give, uniformly over
\(P\in\mathcal M\),
\[
 E_{P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}}[W_n^{\mathrm{ex}}]
 \le\omega_n+2B_Y P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}(R_n^c)
 \le\omega_n+2B_Y|\mathcal X|e^{-np_{\min}/8}.                    \tag{10}
\]
The qualitative exact-grid diameter lemma gives \(\omega_n\to0\), and the
second term in (10) also tends to zero.  This proves the claimed uniform
\(o(1)\) expected width, without assigning it a quantitative rate.
added_lemmas.justification: The theorem supplies a same-assumption inferential improvement: a uniformly honest simultaneous ADRF band whose maximal expected width vanishes uniformly.
added_lemmas.gap: The result is existential and qualitative because compactness gives no explicit inverse modulus for the blind marked channel.
added_lemmas.consumer: It supports consistent whole-curve uncertainty quantification while leaving the sharp \(r_n\) upper and matching marked converse as a separate research program.

proposed.name: \(\mathscr K\)
proposed.construction:
For a Borel probability law \(Q_j\) on \(\mathbb R\), put
\(\phi_{Q_j}(t)=\int e^{itu}\,dQ_j(u)\).  The exact projected nuisance class
\(\mathscr K\) is the set of tuples
\[
 \vartheta=\bigl((p_x,f_x,q_x)_{x\in\mathcal X},Q_1,Q_2\bigr)
\]
such that
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 p_x\ge p_{\min}\quad(x\in\mathcal X),\qquad
 \sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p_x=1,\\
 f_x\in H^\beta(\mathbb R),\quad f_x\ge0,\quad
 \int_{\mathbb R}f_x(a)\,da=1,\quad
 \operatorname{supp}(f_x)\subseteq\mathcal A,\quad
 \|f_x\|_{H^\beta}\le R_f,\quad
 \inf_{a\in I}f_x(a)\ge\kappa,\\
 q_x\in H^\beta(\mathbb R),\quad
 \operatorname{supp}(q_x)\subseteq\mathcal A,\quad
 \|q_x\|_{H^\beta}\le R_q,\quad
 |q_x(a)|\le B_Yf_x(a)\quad(a\in\mathbb R),\\
 \int_{\mathbb R}|u|^{q_e}\,dQ_j(u)\le M_e\quad(j=1,2),\qquad
 \int_{\mathbb R}u\,dQ_2(u)=0,\\
 \inf_{|t|\le\nu_0}|\phi_{Q_j}(t)|\ge c_0
 \quad(j=1,2).
 \end{gathered}
\]
All pointwise signal constraints use the continuous representatives supplied by
\(\beta>1/2\).  The tuple represents the product error law \(Q_1\otimes Q_2\);
it is an outer projection of the full causal class and does not assert that
every one of its elements has a structural causal realization.  For
\(a\in I\), define
\[
 \mu_\vartheta(a)=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p_x\frac{q_x(a)}{f_x(a)}.
\]

proposed_core_edits.reason: The exact outer projection retains every quantitative nuisance restriction needed for channel inversion while not requiring structural realizability of profiled candidates.

proposed.name: \(\Theta^{\mathrm{ex}}_{n,\alpha}\)
proposed.construction:
For a realized sample \(z=(O_1,\ldots,O_n)\), let
\(\Theta^{\mathrm{ex}}_{n,\alpha}(z)\) be the set of all
\(\vartheta\in\mathscr K\) whose mass vector belongs to
\(\mathcal P_{n,\alpha}(z)\) and which, for every
\(x\in\mathcal X\) and \((s,t)\in\mathcal D_n\), obey
\[
 \left|\widehat F_{x,n}(s,t)-
 \widehat f_x(s+t)\phi_{Q_1}(s)\phi_{Q_2}(t)\right|
 \le\rho^F_{x,n}
\]
and
\[
 \left|\widehat G_{x,n}(s,t)-
 \widehat q_x(s+t)\phi_{Q_1}(s)\phi_{Q_2}(t)\right|
 \le\rho^G_{x,n}.
\]
These are exact-class residual constraints: they contain neither spline
Jackson allowances nor atomic approximation allowances.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Removing Jackson and atomic approximation allowances is essential for the compactness-based exact inverse diameter argument.

proposed.name: \(L_n^{\mathrm{ex}},U_n^{\mathrm{ex}}\)
proposed.construction:
If \(\Theta^{\mathrm{ex}}_{n,\alpha}\ne\varnothing\), define, for
\(a\in I\),
\[
 L_n^{\mathrm{ex}}(a)=
 \max\left\{-B_Y,
 \inf_{\vartheta\in\Theta^{\mathrm{ex}}_{n,\alpha}}
 \mu_\vartheta(a)\right\},
 \qquad
 U_n^{\mathrm{ex}}(a)=
 \min\left\{B_Y,
 \sup_{\vartheta\in\Theta^{\mathrm{ex}}_{n,\alpha}}
 \mu_\vartheta(a)\right\}.
\]
If \(\Theta^{\mathrm{ex}}_{n,\alpha}=\varnothing\), set
\(L_n^{\mathrm{ex}}(a)=U_n^{\mathrm{ex}}(a)=0\) for every \(a\in I\).
Put
\[
 \mathcal C_n^{\mathrm{ex}}=(L_n^{\mathrm{ex}},U_n^{\mathrm{ex}}),
 \qquad
 W_n^{\mathrm{ex}}=
 \sup_{a\in I}\{U_n^{\mathrm{ex}}(a)-L_n^{\mathrm{ex}}(a)\}.
\]
This is an abstract infinite-dimensional profiling rule over the exact class
\(\mathscr K\), not a claimed finite algorithm.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Exact profiling needs no ADRF approximation inflation and yields the parallel abstract band required by the maximality directive.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Construct, for compatible strict-interior class indices, one fixed positive density and fixed nonidentical asymmetric error pair together with Bernoulli marked perturbations having the required range, strict Sobolev slack, \(K_n^{1/2-\beta}\) separation, and product-experiment total variation below \(\eta<1-2\alpha\).
open_obligations.obstruction: The frozen index ranges do not ensure a nonempty strict-interior lower submodel: necessarily \(\kappa|I|\le1\) and \(R_f\ge(2B_A)^{-1/2}\), while the allowed endpoint \(c_0=1\) forces every protected-modulus error law to be degenerate and so excludes the required asymmetric compact-spectrum witness. Even after compatible indices are fixed, a Christoffel--Darboux packet must simultaneously preserve the Bernoulli range and Sobolev slack, and the factorial Fourier attenuation must be converted into a weighted chi-square or Hellinger bound for the observed baseline; no frozen result supplies its required lower envelope.
open_obligations.attempted: The moment-annihilation route was carried through the exact marked-channel factorization, yielding factorial attenuation on the fixed frequency square. Direct feasibility checks of the density and error constraints exposed the index obstructions before the total-variation conversion. The conditional all-band testing reduction was separately completed.
open_obligations.partial_result:
Two necessary compatibility conditions follow directly from the frozen class.
Every admissible fixed density must satisfy
\[
 1=\int_{\mathcal A}f_x(a)\,da
 \ge\int_I f_x(a)\,da\ge\kappa|I|,
\]
and Cauchy--Schwarz on \(|\mathcal A|=2B_A\) gives
\[
 R_f\ge\|f_x\|_{H^\beta}\ge\|f_x\|_2
 \ge(2B_A)^{-1/2}.
\]
Neither compatibility inequality is imposed by the displayed index ranges.
At the allowed endpoint \(c_0=1\), the required asymmetric error witness is
also impossible.  Indeed, if \(|E e^{itU}|=1\), equality in the triangle
inequality forces \(e^{itU}\) to be almost surely constant.  Applying this at
two nonzero frequencies in \((-\nu_0,\nu_0)\) having irrational ratio forces
two independent copies of \(U\) to be equal almost surely, hence \(U\) is
degenerate.  Such a law is neither asymmetric in the required witness sense
nor does it have a compactly supported characteristic function.

Conditional on compatible strict-interior fixed nuisances, moment annihilation
does yield the desired analytic attenuation.  If
\(h_n=f(b_{1,n}-b_{0,n})\) satisfies
\(\int a^kh_n(a)\,da=0\) for \(0\le k<K_n\), Taylor's formula and
\(|a|\le B_A\) imply, for \(|u|\le\Omega\),
\[
 |\widehat h_n(u)|
 \le\|h_n\|_1e^{B_A\Omega}
       \frac{(B_A\Omega)^{K_n}}{K_n!}.
\]
For fixed error transforms supported in bounded frequency intervals, the
two-dimensional Fourier transform of the marked observed-density perturbation
is exactly
\[
 \widehat h_n(s+t)\phi_1(s)\phi_2(t),
\]
so it is confined to a fixed square and inherits the factorial attenuation.
The unresolved step is simultaneous construction of a packet having the
Bernoulli-range, strict Sobolev-slack, and
\(K_n^{1/2-\beta}\) separation properties, together with a weighted
chi-square or Hellinger conversion that bounds total variation of the
\(n\)-fold observed experiments.

prose_updates.tldr: This is a statistical-inference paper about a causal ADRF under two blind nonidentical asymmetric replicates. Analytic cocycle identification and an explicit structural response-surface condition establish the causal identifying functional. Two simultaneous bands are separated sharply: an explicit finite relaxed outer-sieve construction is uniformly honest and clipped to \(0\le W_n\le2B_Y\), while an abstract noncomputational exact-class construction is uniformly honest with uniformly \(o(1)\) expected maximal width. Neither construction proves the candidate \(r_n\) rate. The fixed-nuisance Bernoulli lower modulus remains unresolved, so there is no matched honest-band rate.

project_justification.fill: The paper delivers two inference maps. The explicit map uses deterministic spline, frequency, truncation, and atomic dimensions; simultaneous probability-, marked-, and mass-channel radii; relaxed compact outer signal sieves; a joint feasible set; and measurable clipped ADRF extrema. It proves uniform simultaneous coverage and \(0\le W_n\le2B_Y\), but no shrinkage. In parallel, exact empirical-channel residuals are profiled over a compact projected nuisance class. Compactness, expanding-grid equality, and marked cocycle injectivity prove that this abstract exact-class band is uniformly honest and has uniformly \(o(1)\) expected maximal width. The qualitative argument supplies no explicit modulus, and the sharp \(O(r_n)\) upper and matching marked converse remain open.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The explicit conservative procedure uses relaxed order-\(d\) B-spline families for \(f_x,q_x\), finite atomic characteristic-function families for the two errors, and \(p_x\in\mathcal P_{n,\alpha}\) against simultaneous empirical probability- and marked-channel restrictions on \(\mathcal D_n\); its outer splines are feasibility devices rather than asserted model laws. A second, abstract procedure profiles the same empirical radii with no approximation allowances over the exact compact projected class \(\mathscr K\), then takes clipped extrema of \(\mu_{\vartheta}\). The latter is an infinite-dimensional existence construction and is not claimed to be computationally implementable.

prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The causal bridge, analytic-cocycle identification, simultaneous transform concentration, relaxed outer-sieve embedding, and clipped uniform coverage are proved. The finite grid-sieve set has no quantitative inverse modulus and therefore no shrinking-width guarantee. Exact-class compactness does yield a separate uniformly honest band with uniformly \(o(1)\) expected width, but gives no rate, tuning law, or finite algorithm. The sharp-rate program still requires a protected-cube analytic-polynomial confidence construction for both probability and signed marked channels. The fixed-nuisance Bernoulli outcome modulus remains the lower-side obstruction.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The model retains the fixed quantitative restrictions on compact dose support, bounded outcomes, Sobolev radii, overlap, error moments, local spectral modulus, finite-stratum masses, and the structural causal response surface. The explicit finite relaxed outer-sieve band is uniformly honest for all sufficiently large \(n\) and universally clipped to width at most \(2B_Y\), with no proved shrinkage. The parallel exact-class band is abstract and noncomputational; it is uniformly honest and its expected maximal width is uniformly \(o(1)\), but no explicit rate follows. In particular, no \(O(r_n)\), minimax-matching, or rate-elbow claim is made. The matching-converse kernel remains open as \(\mathrm{oeq{:}fixed\text{-}nuisance\text{-}marked\text{-}modulus}\).

statement_notes.consumer: If the marked modulus is resolved, this conditional lower bound would combine with a future \(O(r_n)\) upper theorem to establish the sharp resolution limit; neither the finite conservative band nor the qualitative exact-class band is rate-matching.

proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(n\) at least as large as the common deterministic threshold in
\(\mathrm{lem{:}analytic\text{-}sieve\text{-}stability}\).  We first verify
that the displayed construction is a measurable random band.  At this fixed
\(n\), all coefficient, weight, and atom vectors live in finite-dimensional
Euclidean spaces.  The mass simplex is compact.  The density-spline
constraints are closed, and for every \(f\in\mathscr F_n\), writing
\(f=f_+-f_-\), the constraints in \(\mathrm{def{:}signal\text{-}sieves}\)
give
\[
 \int_{\mathcal A}f_-(a)\,da\le 2B_Aa_{f,n},
 \qquad
 \int_{\mathcal A}f_+(a)\,da
 =\int_{\mathcal A}f(a)\,da+int_{\mathcal A}f_-(a)\,da
 \le 1+4B_Aa_{f,n}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
 \|f\|_{L^1(\mathcal A)}\le 1+6B_Aa_{f,n}.                 \tag{1}
\]
For \(q\in\mathscr Q_n(f)\), its defining envelope and the integral
constraint for \(f\) imply
\[
 \|q\|_{L^1(\mathcal A)}
 \le B_Y\int_{\mathcal A}f(a)\,da
      +2B_A(a_{q,n}+B_Ya_{f,n})
 \le B_Y(1+2B_Aa_{f,n})
      +2B_A(a_{q,n}+B_Ya_{f,n}).                          \tag{2}
\]
On each of the two fixed finite-dimensional spline spaces, equivalence of
norms turns (1) and (2) into bounds on the coefficient vectors.  Hence the
closed signal constraints define compact coefficient sets.  The error-law
constraints define closed subsets of a product of the compact probability
simplex and \([-H_n,H_n]^{M_n}\); the moment, ordering, centering-tolerance,
and protected-modulus restrictions are closed because their defining maps
are continuous.  Thus all deterministic restrictions may be collected in a
compact parameter set \(K_n^\star\).  In particular, every density component
of a point in \(K_n^\star\) obeys
\[
 \inf_{a\in I}f_x(a)\ge \kappa/2,                         \tag{3}
\]
so \((a,\theta)\mapsto\mu_\theta(a)\) is continuous and finite on
\(I\times K_n^\star\).

For a realized sample \(z\), let \(h_n(z,\theta)\) be the maximum of zero
and the positive parts of all sample-dependent mass and channel-constraint
violations in \(\mathrm{def{:}joint\text{-}feasible\text{-}set}\), with the
deterministic restrictions absorbed into \(K_n^\star\).  There are only
finitely many grid constraints, so \(h_n\) is measurable in \(z\) and
continuous in \(\theta\), and
\[
 \Theta_{n,\alpha}(z)
 =\{\theta\in K_n^\star:h_n(z,\theta)=0\}.                \tag{4}
\]
If \(K_n^\star\) is empty, the prescribed empty-set endpoints are identically
zero and hence measurable.  Otherwise choose a countable dense subset
\(K_{n,0}^\star\).  Continuity in \(\theta\) gives
\[
 d_n(z):=\inf_{\theta\in K_n^\star}h_n(z,\theta)
       =\inf_{\theta\in K_{n,0}^\star}h_n(z,\theta),       \tag{5}
\]
so \(d_n\) is measurable, and compactness together with (4) shows that
\(\Theta_{n,\alpha}(z)\ne\varnothing\) exactly when \(d_n(z)=0\).
For each positive integer \(k\), define
\[
 V_{n,k}^+(z,a)
 =\sup_{\theta\in K_n^\star}
   \{\mu_\theta(a)-k h_n(z,\theta)\},
 \qquad
 V_{n,k}^-(z,a)
 =\sup_{\theta\in K_n^\star}
   \{-\mu_\theta(a)-k h_n(z,\theta)\}.                   \tag{6}
\]
Each supremum in (6) equals the supremum over \(K_{n,0}^\star\), and hence
is jointly measurable in \((z,a)\).  On \(\{d_n=0\}\), compactness implies
\[
 V_{n,k}^+(z,a)\downarrow
 \sup_{\theta\in\Theta_{n,\alpha}(z)}\mu_\theta(a),
 \qquad
 V_{n,k}^-(z,a)\downarrow
 -\inf_{\theta\in\Theta_{n,\alpha}(z)}\mu_\theta(a).     \tag{7}
\]
Indeed, a feasible point supplies a lower bound in (6), while continuity on
the compact set bounds \(|\mu_\theta(a)|\).  Therefore any maximizing
sequence \(\theta_k\) satisfies \(h_n(z,\theta_k)=O(k^{-1})\); every
convergent subsequence has a feasible limit by (4), which proves the upper
inequality in (7), and feasible points give the reverse inequality.  The
argument for \(V_{n,k}^-\) is identical.  Equations (5)--(7), together with
the stipulated zero endpoints on \(\{d_n>0\}\), prove joint
sample-and-index measurability of the profiled extrema and hence of \(L_n\)
and \(U_n\).  For each fixed sample with a nonempty feasible set, uniform
continuity of \(\mu_\theta(a)\) on the compact product
\(I\times\Theta_{n,\alpha}(z)\) makes both profiled extrema continuous in
\(a\).  The same is true under the empty-set convention and after clipping.
It follows that \(W_n\) is measurable, since its supremum may be taken over a
fixed countable dense subset of \(I\).

The last assertion of
\(\mathrm{lem{:}analytic\text{-}sieve\text{-}stability}\) now yields, for
every realized sample,
\[
 L_n(a)\le U_n(a)\quad\text{for every }a\in I,
 \qquad 0\le W_n\le 2B_Y.                                  \tag{8}
\]
It remains to prove simultaneous coverage.  Fix \(P\in\mathcal M\).  On
\(\mathcal E_{n,\alpha}\), the same lemma supplies
\(\bar\theta_n\in\Theta_{n,\alpha}\) such that
\[
 \sup_{a\in I}|\mu_{\bar\theta_n}(a)-\mu(a)|\le b_{\mu,n}. \tag{9}
\]
The structural response surface in \(\mathrm{def{:}model\text{-}class}\)
takes values in \([-B_Y,B_Y]\), so
\[
 -B_Y\le \mu(a)=E_P[Y(a)]\le B_Y\qquad(a\in I).           \tag{10}
\]
For every \(a\in I\), feasibility of \(\bar\theta_n\) and (9) give
\[
 \inf_{\theta\in\Theta_{n,\alpha}}\mu_\theta(a)-b_{\mu,n}
 \le \mu_{\bar\theta_n}(a)-b_{\mu,n}
 \le \mu(a),                                               \tag{11}
\]
and
\[
 \sup_{\theta\in\Theta_{n,\alpha}}\mu_\theta(a)+b_{\mu,n}
 \ge \mu_{\bar\theta_n}(a)+b_{\mu,n}
 \ge \mu(a).                                               \tag{12}
\]
In (11), both arguments of the maximum defining \(L_n(a)\) are at most
\(\mu(a)\), by (10); in (12), both arguments of the minimum defining
\(U_n(a)\) are at least \(\mu(a)\).  Thus the clipping preserves coverage
and
\[
 \mathcal E_{n,\alpha}
 \subseteq
 \{L_n(a)\le\mu(a)\le U_n(a)\text{ for every }a\in I\}.   \tag{13}
\]
The uniform event bound in
\(\mathrm{lem{:}analytic\text{-}sieve\text{-}stability}\) and (13) imply
\[
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal M}P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}
 \{L_n(a)\le\mu(a)\le U_n(a)\text{ for every }a\in I\}
 \ge 1-\alpha.                                             \tag{14}
\]
Joint measurability, endpoint ordering in (8), and (14) are precisely the
requirements of \(\mathrm{def{:}honest\text{-}bands}\), so
\(\mathcal C_n\in\mathfrak B_{n,\alpha}\).  Finally, (8) and monotonicity
of expectation yield
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M}
 E_{P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}}[W_n]\le 2B_Y.            \tag{15}
\]
The threshold used above is the one supplied uniformly by the stability
lemma, hence depends only on \(\alpha\) and the fixed class indices.  No
shrinking inverse-diameter or rate assertion is used in (1)--(15).
